name: Sony
description: Japanese consumer electronics giant with one of the broadest headphone catalogs in the world, spanning budget earbuds to the flagship MDR-Z1R and the iconic MDR-7506 studio standard.

name: Sennheiser
description: German audio institution whose HD 600 series defined the reference open-back standard for a generation. The HD 800 and Orpheus HE-1 represent the outer edge of what headphones can achieve.

name: Philips
description: Dutch electronics multinational whose Fidelio line produced several acclaimed audiophile headphones before the brand shifted focus toward consumer electronics.

name: Audio-Technica
description: Japanese precision manufacturer best known for the ATH-M50x studio monitor and a deep catalog of open-back headphones from the AD and R series.

name: AKG
description: Viennese studio legend whose K 240 and K 701 shaped professional monitoring for decades. Now owned by Samsung/Harman but the K 812 and K 872 keep the legacy alive.

name: Beyerdynamic
description: Century-old German manufacturer and inventor of the dynamic headphone driver. The DT 770/880/990 trilogy and Tesla-driver flagships are benchmarks of German engineering precision.

name: Bose
description: Massachusetts-based acoustics company that popularised active noise cancellation with the QuietComfort line. Prioritises comfort, convenience, and accessible sound quality.

name: Audeze
description: California planar magnetic specialist that brought the technology to mainstream audiophiles with the LCD series. Their SLAM magnet arrays set efficiency records for planar design.

name: HiFiMan
description: Chinese planar pioneer founded by Dr. Fang Bian. Responsible for democratising planar magnetic headphones and producing the Susvara, widely considered one of the finest headphones ever made.

name: Focal
description: French speaker manufacturer whose entry into headphones with the Utopia and Elear reshaped the high-end market. Known for beryllium-domed drivers and premium cabinet-grade materials.

name: Bowers & Wilkins
description: British hi-fi institution whose Px series brought premium wireless to a design-conscious audience. The P9 Signature remains a statement piece for the brand.

name: Grado
description: Brooklyn family business spanning three generations, making supra-aural open-back headphones by hand since the 1950s. Unmistakable sound, unmistakable look.

name: Meze Audio
description: Romanian boutique that stunned the audiophile world with the 99 Classics in 2015 and followed up with the Empyrean — a flagship using Rinaro's isodynamic planar driver.

name: Dan Clark Audio
description: San Diego workshop founded as MrSpeakers. Known for T50RP modifications that evolved into original planar designs including the Ether and STEALTH.

name: Apple
description: Cupertino technology company whose AirPods Max brought Apple's design language and computational audio to the over-ear headphone market.

name: Beats
description: Brand founded by Dr. Dre and Jimmy Iovine that made headphones a fashion accessory. Acquired by Apple in 2014 and now integrates Apple silicon for spatial audio.

name: Shure
description: Chicago microphone and audio equipment company whose SRH line is a studio workhorse. The SRH1540 and SRH1840 are respected reference tools.

name: SteelSeries
description: Danish gaming peripherals brand whose Arctis series redefined the gaming headset with ski-goggle headbands and a focus on comfort for long sessions.

name: HyperX
description: Kingston's gaming brand, producing the Cloud series of studio-driver-based headsets that punched well above their price. Now owned by HP.

name: Razer
description: Gaming hardware brand from San Francisco. The Kraken and BlackShark V2 series are popular esports headsets; the Opus line targets lifestyle listeners.

name: Logitech G
description: Swiss peripherals giant whose G Pro X series used Blue Microphone technology and swappable drivers to target competitive gamers.

name: Astro Gaming
description: Console gaming headset specialist whose A40 TR and A50 Wireless are fixtures in professional esports broadcasting setups. Owned by Logitech.

name: Turtle Beach
description: Veteran gaming headset maker that pioneered surround-sound processing in console headsets. The Stealth series remains a popular mid-tier choice.

name: Corsair
description: PC hardware company whose Virtuoso series targets PC gamers with high-resolution audio and premium build quality.

name: ASUS ROG
description: Republic of Gamers division of ASUS, producing gaming headsets with aggressive styling and ESS DAC-equipped USB audio.

name: Abyss
description: Upstate New York boutique producing the AB-1266, a flagship open planar headphone with a bold industrial design that has no counterpart on the market.

name: ZMF Headphones
description: Chicago one-man operation by Zach Mehrbach building handcrafted wood-cupped dynamic and planar headphones. Long lead times, devoted following.

name: Stax
description: The definitive electrostatic headphone maker, producing earspeakers since 1938. The SR-009 and SR-X9000 are considered the purest transducers available at any price.

name: Final Audio
description: Japanese audio laboratory known for unconventional acoustic engineering. The D8000 planar and Sonorous series are boundary-pushing products from a deeply research-driven company.

name: Fostex
description: Japanese driver manufacturer whose T50RP became the most-modded headphone in audiophile history, and whose TH900 series uses biodynamic technology.

name: Denon
description: Japanese audio institution whose AH-D series closed-backs use biodynamic 50mm drivers. The D9200 with its nano-fibre diaphragm is a standout statement product.

name: Rosson Audio
description: Small-batch planar workshop by Alex Rosson, co-founder of Audeze. The RAD-0 is a hand-made statement piece with custom wood cups.

name: Kennerton
description: St. Petersburg audio atelier building planar magnetic flagships in exotic wood housings. The Odin and Thror are among the most beautiful headphones made.

name: Ultrasone
description: Bavarian company behind the S-Logic spatial driver technology, which positions the driver off-axis to reduce ear canal pressure and create a wider perceived soundstage.

name: Bang & Olufsen
description: Danish luxury electronics brand whose Beoplay H line is as much furniture as audio equipment. The H95 is their flagship closed-back, built from aluminium and lambskin.

name: Sonos
description: Wireless audio company that entered headphones with the Ace, combining spatial audio and SoundSwap for seamless transition between speakers and headphones.

name: Marshall
description: Iconic amplifier brand that extended into headphones in 2010. The Major series on-ear design channels the brand's rock heritage into a consumer-friendly product line.

name: JBL
description: American speaker company under Harman. The Live and Club series cover premium consumer wireless while the Professional line serves studio monitoring.

name: Skullcandy
description: Park City, Utah brand that brought bold colour and skate/snowboard culture to headphones. The Crusher series with haptic bass is a signature product.

name: Anker Soundcore
description: Anker's audio sub-brand producing aggressively priced wireless headphones with competitive ANC. The Space Q45 punches well above its category.

name: Technics
description: Panasonic's premium audio brand revived in 2014. The EAH-A800 wireless headphone brings hi-fi DNA to the ANC market with LDAC and multipoint connectivity.

name: Nothing
description: Carl Pei's London tech startup known for transparent industrial design. The Headphone (1) was their first over-ear, applying the brand's distinctive dot-matrix aesthetic.

name: Koss
description: Milwaukee company that invented the stereo headphone in 1958. The Porta Pro has been in continuous production since 1984 and remains a cult favourite.

name: V-Moda
description: Lifestyle and DJ headphone brand from Val Kolton, known for the indestructible Crossfade M-100 and a custom shield programme allowing personalised engravings.

name: Yamaha
description: Musical instrument giant with a deep headphone catalog. The YH-5000SE flagship uses an orthodynamic driver derived from their 1970s HP-1 and is made in Japan.

name: Pioneer
description: Japanese AV brand whose Pioneer DJ division produces the HDJ series, professional turntablist monitors trusted by DJs worldwide.

name: AIAIAI
description: Copenhagen brand whose TMA-2 is the world's most modular headphone — mix and match 360 components including drivers, earpads, headbands, and cables.

name: 1More
description: Shenzhen brand tuned in collaboration with Grammy-winning engineers. The SonoFlow series delivers wireless ANC at prices that embarrass the competition.

name: Edifier
description: Beijing audio company whose STAX Spirit line brought planar magnetic technology to mid-range wireless headphones at an accessible price.

name: Cleer
description: San Diego audio brand founded by ex-JBL engineers. The Alpha uses a custom 40mm driver and targets audiophile-grade wireless performance.

name: Austrian Audio
description: Vienna studio founded by ex-AKG engineers after the AKG Vienna facility closed. The Hi-X55 and Hi-X65 are direct spiritual successors to AKG's studio heritage.

name: Neumann
description: The microphone company's headphone line is aimed squarely at mastering engineers. The NDH 20 and NDH 30 offer exceptional tonal accuracy for critical listening.

name: Moondrop
description: Chengdu IEM specialist that expanded into over-ear planars with the Venus and Para. Known for anime-inspired packaging and technically rigorous tuning based on the HRTF target.

name: Sivga
description: Chinese wood-specialist headphone maker crafting dynamic closed-backs with real rosewood, walnut, and zebrawood housings at accessible prices.

name: Sendy Audio
description: Planar magnetic specialist using 97mm drivers in open-back designs. The Peacock and Aiva target the audiophile mid-fi market with premium build quality.

name: FiiO
description: Guangzhou portable audio giant best known for DACs and DAPs. The FT3 and FT5 represent their serious push into full-size headphones with large dynamic and planar drivers.

name: Spirit Torino
description: Turin boutique producing ultra-light open-back headphones designed for comfortable all-day listening. The Super Leggera is one of the lightest audiophile headphones available.

name: Warwick Acoustics
description: British electrostatic specialist producing the Sonoma Model One and Aperio — complete systems with proprietary energisers built from aerospace-grade materials.

name: Mark Levinson
description: American high-end audio brand whose No. 5909 wireless headphone brings luxury materials and Hi-Res Audio certification to the travel headphone market.

name: T+A
description: Herford high-end manufacturer whose Solitaire P planar headphone features a 200mm driver array and is designed to pair with their in-house headphone amplifiers.

name: HEDD Audio
description: Berlin studio monitor company whose HEDDphone uses Air Motion Transformer drivers — folded-membrane technology borrowed from loudspeakers for exceptionally fast transient response.

name: Grell Audio
description: Founded by Axel Grell, chief developer of the Sennheiser HD 800. The OAE1 open-air earspeaker is his attempt to solve headphone imaging from first principles.

name: Ollo Audio
description: Slovenian studio headphone maker offering individually tested and calibrated closed and open-back monitors, with measurement graphs shipped with each unit.

name: Monoprice
description: Direct-to-consumer electronics brand whose Monolith M1060 planar brought 106mm drivers to an audience that couldn't afford Audeze prices.

name: Superlux
description: Taiwanese professional audio equipment maker whose HD 668B and HD 681 are studio-standard monitors in disguise, widely used in Chinese broadcast facilities.

name: Samson
description: New York professional audio brand whose SR850 semi-open monitor is a rebranded Superlux HD 668B — one of the most recommended budget headphones in audiophile communities.

name: Status Audio
description: Direct-to-consumer brand cutting out retail markups. The CB-1 closed-back became a breakout product in the budget audiophile market.

name: Jabra
description: GN Audio's communications headset brand trusted in enterprise and contact centre environments. The Evolve2 series is engineered for all-day wearing comfort.

name: Harman Kardon
description: American audio brand known for premium design. The SOHO on-ear represents a premium lifestyle offering combining Harman's speaker tuning with a portable form factor.

name: Oppo
description: Californian electronics company whose PM-1 and PM-3 planar headphones were critically acclaimed before the brand's closure in 2018. Now sought-after on the used market.

name: Creative
description: Singapore technology company whose Sound Blaster brand shaped PC audio. The Aurvana Live! uses a biodynamic driver co-developed with Foster Electric.

name: Rode
description: Sydney microphone company whose NTH-100 studio headphone was developed with DSP-calibrated tuning via the NTH-Mic measurement system.

name: Klipsch
description: Arkansas speaker company whose Heritage HP-3 headphone uses a wooden cup design inspired by their classic horn-loaded loudspeakers.

name: RAAL
description: Ribbon driver specialist producing the SR1a — a headphone that uses a true ribbon transducer and requires a special interface for conventional amplifier connection.

name: HarmonicDyne
description: Chengdu audiophile brand producing the G200, a large-scale open planar headphone with a distinctive hexagonal driver architecture.

name: PSB
description: Canadian speaker company whose M4U series headphones apply speaker engineering principles and active Room Feel correction to headphone acoustics.

name: E-Mu
description: California synthesiser pioneer whose headphone line used biodynamic drivers co-developed with Foster Electric. The Teak and Rosewood are now collector items.

name: Audioquest
description: Cable and accessory specialist whose NightOwl and NightHawk used Foster biodynamic drivers in carbon fibre and wood housings before the line was discontinued.

name: NAD
description: Canadian electronics brand whose VISO HP50 used RoomFeel target curve technology — an early attempt to apply room-corrected tuning to headphone listening.

name: Brainwavz
description: Hong Kong audio brand best known for replacement earpads compatible with hundreds of headphones, and the HM5 studio monitor.

name: Modhouse Audio
description: Wisconsin modification workshop building the Argon — a T50RP Mk2 base fitted with a proprietary driver tuned for a warm, musical presentation. Waitlists measured in months.

name: Kiwi Ears
description: Young Chinese audio brand with rapid product cadence. The Ardor open planar earned strong reviews at its price, drawing comparisons to headphones costing three times as much.

name: Plantronics
description: Communications headset pioneer whose BackBeat line brought Bluetooth comfort to the office market. Merged with Polycom to form Poly, now part of HP.

name: Phiaton
description: Korean premium audio brand producing the MS 530 — one of the earliest commercially successful wireless ANC headphones with Bluetooth at launch.

name: Teufel
description: Berlin direct-sales speaker brand whose Real Blue NC offers competitive ANC performance at prices below the major consumer brands.

name: House of Marley
description: Bob Marley estate brand producing headphones from sustainable materials including bamboo, hemp, and recycled plastics. Donates to environmental causes.

name: Cooler Master
description: PC cooling and peripheral brand whose MH751 became a surprise hit in gaming headset communities for its studio-driver-based sound quality at a modest price.

name: JVC
description: Victor Company of Japan, known for the HA-DX1000 and HA-DX2000 mahogany wood-cup flagship closed-backs and the HA-SW series isodynamic planars.

name: Tago Studio
description: Small Japanese studio headphone maker offering individually serial-numbered monitors using high-powered 1.5T Neodymium drivers. Made in Japan.

name: Takstar
description: Guangzhou professional audio company whose Pro 80 is the OEM basis for many rebranded studio monitors worldwide. The HF580 planar punches above its category.

name: Goldplanar
description: Chinese planar magnetic specialist producing the GL2000 — a dual-sided planar with a 68mm driver that delivers competitive performance at a budget price.

name: MySphere
description: Vienna-based audio engineering project by Heinz Renner, former chief engineer at AKG. The MySphere 3 is the spiritual successor to the AKG K1000 open-air earspeaker.

name: Panasonic
description: Japanese electronics conglomerate with a modest headphone catalog. The RP-HD10 is their most audiophile-focused recent offering.

name: Crosszone
description: Niche Japanese brand producing headphones with built-in acoustic crossfeed. The CZ-1 uses secondary in-ear drivers to simulate the inter-channel crosstalk of loudspeaker listening.
